messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered: High latency SLO burn detected for route /v1/generate on api.redwood-inference.com. p95 > 2.5s, p99 > 5.0s for last 5m. Paging on-call.
PagerDuty: PagerDuty incident #PD-8421 — page fired to schedule 'sre-rotation' (priority: P2).
Alex: acked (on-call) — looking. Opening runbook.
Alex: first quick check — errors stable, no spikes in 5xx. Looks like per-token latency spike.
Sam: grabbing prometheus graphs now. Query: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))` returns p95 ~ 2.8s, p99 ~ 5.6s, baseline ~0.6s.
Maria: any recent deploys? I see a runtime push to inference-runtime-main ~10m ago (rev: r-2026-03-14-21). Could be related.
Alex: good catch. Correlating deployment timeline with latency spike.
Alex: mitigation options: 1) rollback runtime; 2) increase replica count / add warm pool; 3) route traffic to older model variant. Which is lowest friction?
Sam: quick mitigation — scale up replicas for the affected pool and enable fallback routing to 'model-4-small' temporarily. I'll open the scaling patch.
Sam: running `kubectl -n inference scale deployment inference-pool --replicas=12` now.
OpsRunbookBot: Runbook step executed: scaled inference-pool from 6 -> 12 replicas (initiated by Sam). Monitor for 2m.
Alex: monitoring… p95 dropping to 1.5s after ~60s, p99 still ~3.8s. Improvement but not fully recovered.
Maria: stepping in to rollback runtime if needed. Preparing rollback patch: `deployctl rollback inference-runtime-main r-2026-03-13-97`. Will hold for 2m unless Alex requests.
Alex: hold off for now — scaling helped partial. Can we enable cached KV/prefix cache for hot prompts?
Sam: enabling prefix cache flag for high-throughput model groups: `POST /api/admin/cache/enable?group=hot-prompts`. Doing now.
IncidentBot: Action applied: prefix cache enabled for group hot-prompts by Sam.
Alex: p95 ~1.0s now, p99 ~2.1s. Good. Customer impact: roughly 12% of requests saw noticeable latency increase; no user-facing errors reported, but interactive features experienced lag.
PagerDuty: PagerDuty note: incident acknowledged by Alex, escalation deferred.
Maria: still want to open a rollback ticket and run a canary of the old runtime in parallel — we should avoid full rollback until postmortem.
Alex: agreed. I'll keep incident open and handoff to Jonah for the night shift. Jonah — quick summary: scaling+cache mitigated immediate burn; root cause likely regression in r-2026-03-14-21 runtime path affecting KV-cache miss/hot-path kernel selection.
Jonah: taking handoff — ack. I'll keep monitoring p95/p99 for next 3 hours, and coordinate rollback if we see re-burn.
Alex: handing off -> @Jonah. Add to incident timeline: actions taken, metrics, and links to runbook + dashboard.
Sam: created dashboard snapshot: https://dashboards.redwood/inference/PD-8421-snapshot and a short log snippet: ```
[21:04:12] req_id=abc123 duration=5.42s model=model-4 kernel=quantized-v2 cache_hit=false
[21:04:17] req_id=def456 duration=4.98s model=model-4 kernel=quantized-v2 cache_hit=false
```
Maria: filing a post-incident ticket against runtime team: JIRA INF-2972. Tagging @runtime-team.
Alex: thanks all. Closing note: severity P2, customer impact moderate (latency only), no data loss. Follow-ups: update runbook with runtime canary checklist, add better kernel-selection alarms, and test prefix-cache warmup during deploys.
Jonah: will run watch and report any regressions. If p99 > 4.5s for >10m, escalate and execute rollback.
IncidentBot: Incident #PD-8421 — status: monitored (assigned to Jonah).
Alex: moving to postmortem channel for write-up, leaving this thread open until next update. :thumbsup:
